title: PostgreSQL: JSONB subscription syntax missing parentheses for JSONB-returning functions

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/12777
Originally posted by **noirbee** August 1, 2025 Following https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/10927 and https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/2ac0c459669d0200a4d15162ffc0a8765c60cb07 , upgrading to sqlalchemy 2.0.42 now triggers syntax errors on PostgreSQL's side when using JSONB-returning functions, e.g. `jsonb_array_elements()`. This is due to a quirk in PostgreSQL's own syntax, where the `["key"]`-style JSONB subscription cannot be used as readily as the `->` / `->>` one. A good example is worth a thousand words: ``` postgres=# SELECT jsonb_array_elements('[{"key": "value1"}, {"key": "value2"}]'::jsonb) -> 'key'; -- good old "->" syntax, no parentheses needed ?column? ---------- "value1" "value2" (2 rows) postgres=# SELECT jsonb_array_elements('[{"key": "value1"}, {"key": "value2"}]'::jsonb) ['key']; -- no parentheses around jsonb_array_elements(), fail ERROR: syntax error at or near "[" LINE 1: ...ts('[{"key": "value1"}, {"key": "value2"}]'::jsonb) ['key']; ^ postgres=# SELECT (jsonb_array_elements('[{"key": "value1"}, {"key": "value2"}]'::jsonb)) ['key']; -- parentheses around jsonb_array_elements(), OK jsonb_array_elements ---------------------- "value1" "value2" (2 rows) ``` Since 2ac0c459669d0200a4d15162ffc0a8765c60cb07, sqlalchemy now uses the `['key']` syntax everywhere; in most cases (i.e. JSONB column subscription) this pauses no problem, but when using functions with an explicit `type_=JSONB` it now always generates statement using the new syntax, which may fail. ```python # sqla_postgresql_jsonb_subscript.py from sqlalchemy import __version__, func from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass class Hello(Base): __tablename__ = "hello" id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True) data = mapped_column(postgresql.JSONB) print("sqlalchemy", __version__) for statement in ( Hello.data["my_array"], func.jsonb_array_elements(Hello.data["my_array"], type_=postgresql.JSONB), func.jsonb_array_elements(Hello.data["my_array"], type_=postgresql.JSONB)["key"], ): print(statement.compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect())) ``` In SQLAlchemy 2.0.41: ```shell % ./venv/bin/python sqla_postgresql_jsonb_subscript.py sqlalchemy 2.0.41 hello.data -> %(data_1)s jsonb_array_elements(hello.data -> %(data_1)s) jsonb_array_elements((hello.data -> %(data_1)s)) -> %(jsonb_array_elements_1)s ``` In SQLAlchemy 2.0.42: ```shell % ./venv/bin/python sqla_postgresql_jsonb_subscript.py sqlalchemy 2.0.42 hello.data[%(data_1)s] jsonb_array_elements(hello.data[%(data_1)s]) jsonb_array_elements(hello.data[%(data_1)s])[%(jsonb_array_elements_1)s] ``` The following patch seems to fix the issue, but I'm not proficient in SQLA's guts to be sure it actually does the trick: ```diff --- venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/base.py.orig 2025-08-01 14:47:38.795511847 +0200 +++ venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/base.py 2025-08-01 14:49:13.244293085 +0200 @@ -1887,7 +1887,7 @@ ): # for pg14+JSONB use subscript notation: col['key'] instead # of col -> 'key' - return "%s[%s]" % ( + return "(%s)[%s]" % ( self.process(binary.left, **kw), self.process(binary.right, **kw), ) ```
